newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp says welcomes stability pact deal.
newsitem.headline: Krupp says welcomes stability pact deal.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Tuesday that he welcomed approval of the stability pact in Amsterdam on Monday.
"I welcome the affirmation of the stability pact and the chapter on unemployment," Krupp said adding, "I view this agreement as very sensible."
Krupp was addressing a conference organised by the OeTV public sector transport union.
Krupp described the stability pact as "mainly an instrument to further appease the German side."
The stability pact, brainchild of German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, is designed to ensure that European nations maintain fiscal discipline once the single currency area starts in January 1999.
"The agreement is not so surprising. It is a sign of European prudence."
Krupp also said he saw good chances for a stable euro, the future European single currency.
